sanskrit: śaineyaṃ śaravarṣāṇi vikirantaṃ samantataḥ abhyayāt kauravo rājan bhūriḥ saṃgrāmamūrdhani
english: As the grandson of Śini was scattering showers of arrows on every side, O king, the Kaurava Bhūri rushed upon him at the forefront of the battle.

sanskrit: sahadevam athāyāntaṃ droṇaprepsuṃ mahāratham karṇo vaikartano rājan vārayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: And as Sahadeva, that great chariot-warrior, came on, eager to reach Droṇa, Karṇa the son of Vikartana, O king, held back that son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: bhīmasenam athāyāntaṃ vyāditāsyam ivāntakam svayaṃ duryodhano yuddhe pratīpaṃ mṛtyum āvrajat
english: And as Bhīmasena advanced like Death with jaws gaping wide, Duryodhana himself went forth in the fight to meet him, as one goes to meet hostile Death.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ ca yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvayuddhaviśāradam śakuniḥ saubalo rājan vārayām āsa satvaraḥ
english: And as Nakula, the foremost of warriors, skilled in every mode of combat, advanced, Śakuni the son of Subala, O king, swiftly held him in check.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinam athāyāntaṃ rathena rathināṃ varam kṛpo śāradvato rājan vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: And as Śikhaṇḍin, the best of chariot-warriors, came on in his car, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat, O king, withstood him in the battle.

sanskrit: prativindhyam athāyāntaṃ mayūrasadṛśair hayaiḥ duḥśāsano mahārāja yatto yattam avārayat
english: And as Prativindhya advanced with horses hued like peacocks, Duḥśāsana, O great king, straining himself, held back that straining foe.

sanskrit: bhaimasenim athāyāntaṃ māyāśataviśāradam aśvatthāmā pitur mānaṃ kurvāṇaḥ pratyaṣedhayat
english: And as the son of Bhīmasena advanced, expert in a hundred illusions, Aśvatthāman, upholding his father's honour, drove him back.

sanskrit: drupadaṃ vṛṣasenas tu sasainyaṃ sapadānugam vārayām āsa samare droṇaprepsuṃ mahāratham
english: And Vṛṣasena held back in battle Drupada, that great chariot-warrior, together with his troops and his foot-soldiers, as he sought to reach Droṇa.

sanskrit: virāṭaṃ drutam āyāntaṃ droṇasya nidhanaṃ prati madrarājaḥ susaṃkruddho vārayām āsa bhārata
english: And as Virāṭa came on swiftly, bent upon Droṇa's death, the king of the Madras, greatly enraged, held him in check, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: śatānīkam athāyāntaṃ nākuliṃ rabhasaṃ raṇe citraseno rurodhāśu śarair droṇavadhepsayā
english: And as Śatānīka, the son of Nakula, advanced impetuously in the fray, desiring Droṇa's slaughter, Citrasena swiftly checked him with his shafts.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ ca yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ prādravantaṃ mahāratham alambuso mahārāja rākṣasendro nyavārayat
english: And as Arjuna, the foremost of warriors, that mighty chariot-fighter, came rushing on, Alambusa, O great king, the lord of the Rākṣasas, held him back.

sanskrit: tathā droṇaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ nighnantaṃ śātravān raṇe dhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha pāñcālyo hṛṣṭarūpam avārayat
english: And as Droṇa, that mighty bowman, was slaying his foes in the battle, Dhṛṣṭadyumna the Pāñcāla, with a joyful mien, withstood him.

sanskrit: tathānyān pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ samāyātān mahārathān tāvakā rathino rājan vārayām āsur ojasā
english: And the other great chariot-warriors of the sons of Pāṇḍu who came on, your own car-warriors, O king, withstood with all their might.

sanskrit: gajārohā gajais tūrṇaṃ saṃnipatya mahāmṛdhe yodhayantaḥ sma dṛśyante śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Riders of elephants, swiftly closing with their elephants in that great battle, were seen to fight by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: niśīthe turagā rājann ādravantaḥ parasparam samadṛśyanta vegena pakṣavanta ivādrayaḥ
english: At midnight, O king, the horses, charging at one another, were seen rushing on with speed like winged mountains.

sanskrit: sādinaḥ sādibhiḥ sārdhaṃ prāsaśaktyṛṣṭipāṇayaḥ samāgacchan mahārāja vinadantaḥ pṛthak pṛthak
english: Horsemen, with lances, javelins, and spears in hand, closed with horsemen, O great king, each roaring out his own war-cry.

sanskrit: narās tu bahavas tatra samājagmuḥ parasparam gadābhir musalaiś caiva nānāśastraiś ca saṃghaśaḥ
english: And many men there met one another in throngs, with maces and clubs and weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu hārdikyo dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram vārayām āsa saṃkruddho velevodvṛttam arṇavam
english: And Kṛtavarman the son of Hṛdika, full of wrath, held back Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, as the shore holds back the surging sea.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu hārdikyaṃ viddhvā pañcabhir āśugaiḥ punar vivyādha viṃśatyā tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira, having pierced the son of Hṛdika with five swift arrows, struck him again with twenty, and cried, 'Stand! Stand!'

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu saṃkruddho dharmaputrasya māriṣa dhanuś ciccheda bhallena taṃ ca vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: But Kṛtavarman, greatly enraged, O sire, cut off with a broad-headed shaft the bow of the son of Dharma, and pierced him with seven.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ hārdikyaṃ daśabhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Then taking up another bow, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma planted ten arrows in the arms and breast of the son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: mādhavas tu raṇe viddho dharmaputreṇa māriṣa prākampata ca roṣeṇa saptabhiś cārdayac charaiḥ
english: And the Mādhava, thus pierced in battle by the son of Dharma, O sire, trembled with rage and afflicted him with seven shafts.

sanskrit: tasya pārtho dhanuś chittvā hastāvāpaṃ nikṛtya ca prāhiṇon niśitān bāṇān pañca rājañ śilāśitān
english: The son of Pṛthā, cutting off his bow and severing his leather glove, sped at him five whetted arrows, sharpened on stone, O king.

sanskrit: te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā hemacitraṃ mahādhanam prāviśan dharaṇīm ugrā valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Those fierce shafts, piercing his gold-wrought, costly armour, entered the earth like serpents entering an anthill.

sanskrit: akṣṇor nimeṣamātreṇa so 'nyad ādāya kārmukam vivyādha pāṇḍavaṃ ṣaṣṭyā sūtaṃ ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: In the mere twinkling of the eyes, taking up another bow, he pierced the son of Pāṇḍu with sixty arrows and his charioteer with nine.

sanskrit: tasya śaktim ameyātmā pāṇḍavo bhujagopamām cikṣepa bharataśreṣṭha rathe nyasya mahad dhanuḥ
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu, of immeasurable soul, laying his great bow upon his car, hurled at him a dart like a serpent, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sā hemacitrā mahatī pāṇḍavena praveritā nirbhidya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ prāviśad dharaṇītalam
english: That great dart, adorned with gold, flung by the son of Pāṇḍu, piercing his right arm, entered the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu gṛhya pārthaḥ punar dhanuḥ hārdikyaṃ chādayām āsa śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: At that very moment, the son of Pṛthā, taking up his bow again, covered the son of Hṛdika with arrows of smooth joints.

sanskrit: tatas tu samare śūro vṛṣṇīnāṃ pravaro rathī vyaśvasūtarathaṃ cakre nimeṣārdhād yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Then in the battle that hero, the foremost car-warrior of the Vṛṣṇis, in half the twinkling of an eye made Yudhiṣṭhira bereft of horses, charioteer, and car.

sanskrit: tatas tu pāṇḍavo jyeṣṭhaḥ khaḍgacarma samādade tad asya niśitair bāṇair vyadhaman mādhavo raṇe
english: Then the eldest son of Pāṇḍu took up sword and shield; but the Mādhava shattered them with his whetted shafts in the fight.

sanskrit: tomaraṃ tu tato gṛhya svarṇadaṇḍaṃ durāsadam preṣayat samare tūrṇaṃ hārdikyasya yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then taking up a gold-shafted, irresistible lance, Yudhiṣṭhira swiftly sped it in the battle at the son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā dharmarājabhujacyutam dvidhā ciccheda hārdikyaḥ kṛtahastaḥ smayann iva
english: As it came hurtling, loosed from the arm of the king of righteousness, the deft-handed son of Hṛdika cut it in two, as if with a smile.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatenājau dharmaputram avākirat kavacaṃ cāsya saṃkruddhaḥ śarais tīkṣṇair adārayat
english: Then in the fight he covered the son of Dharma with a hundred arrows, and in his wrath rent his armour with his sharp shafts.

sanskrit: hārdikyaśarasaṃchinnaṃ kavacaṃ tan mahātmanaḥ vyaśīryata raṇe rājaṃs tārājālam ivāmbarāt
english: That armour of the high-souled one, cut through by the shafts of the son of Hṛdika, fell apart in the battle, O king, like a net of stars falling from the sky.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā virathaḥ śīrṇavarmā śarārditaḥ apāyāsīd raṇāt tūrṇaṃ dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: With his bow cut off, deprived of his car, his armour shattered, tormented by arrows, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma swiftly withdrew from the battle.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu nirjitya dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram punar droṇasya jugupe cakram eva mahābalaḥ
english: And Kṛtavarman, of great strength, having vanquished Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma, once more guarded the wheel of Droṇa's car.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhūris tu samare rājañ śaineyaṃ rathināṃ varam āpatantam apāsedhat prapānād iva kuñjaram
english: Saṃjaya said: But Bhūri in the battle, O king, drove back the grandson of Śini, that best of car-warriors, as he rushed on, even as one turns an elephant from the watering-place.

sanskrit: athainaṃ sātyakiḥ kruddhaḥ pañcabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha hṛdaye tūrṇaṃ prāsravat tasya śoṇitam
english: Then Sātyaki, enraged, swiftly pierced him in the heart with five whetted shafts, and his blood gushed forth.

sanskrit: tathaiva kauravo yuddhe śaineyaṃ yuddhadurmadam daśabhir viśikhais tīkṣṇair avidhyata bhujāntare
english: In the same way the Kaurava, in the fight, pierced the grandson of Śini, that warrior intoxicated with battle, with ten sharp arrows between the shoulders.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ mahārāja tatakṣāte śarair bhṛśam krodhasaṃraktanayanau krodhād visphārya kārmuke
english: The two of them, O great king, gashed each other sorely with arrows, their eyes red with rage, twanging their bows in their fury.

sanskrit: tayor āsīn mahārāja śastravṛṣṭiḥ sudāruṇā kruddhayoḥ sāyakamucor yamāntakanikāśayoḥ
english: There arose between those two, O great king, a most dreadful rain of weapons, as in their wrath they loosed their shafts, resembling Yama the destroyer.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ śarai rājan pracchādya samare sthitau muhūrtaṃ caiva tad yuddhaṃ samarūpam ivābhavat
english: Covering each other with arrows, O king, they stood firm in the battle, and for a while their combat seemed evenly matched.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja śaineyaḥ prahasann iva dhanuś ciccheda samare kauravyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then the grandson of Śini, enraged, O great king, as if smiling, cut off in the battle the bow of the high-souled Kaurava.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha hṛdaye tūrṇaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Then, as he was bereft of his bow, he swiftly pierced him in the heart with nine whetted shafts, and cried, 'Stand! Stand!'

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā śatruṇā śatrutāpanaḥ dhanur anyat samādāya sātvataṃ pratyavidhyata
english: Deeply pierced by his powerful foe, that scorcher of foes took up another bow and pierced the Sātvata in return.

sanskrit: sa viddhvā sātvataṃ bāṇais tribhir eva viśāṃ pate dhanuś ciccheda bhallena sutīkṣṇena hasann iva
english: Having pierced the Sātvata with three arrows, O lord of peoples, he cut off his bow with a very sharp broad-headed shaft, as if laughing.

sanskrit: chinnadhanvā mahārāja sātyakiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ prajahāra mahāvegāṃ śaktiṃ tasya mahorasi
english: His bow severed, O great king, Sātyaki, swooning with rage, hurled at his broad breast a dart of great velocity.

sanskrit: sa tu śaktyā vibhinnāṅgo nipapāta rathottamāt lohitāṅga ivākāśād dīptaraśmir yadṛcchayā
english: His body cleft by that dart, he fell from his excellent car, like the ruddy-bodied planet Mars, with its blazing rays, falling by chance from the sky.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā hataṃ śūram aśvatthāmā mahārathaḥ abhyadhāvata vegena śaineyaṃ prati saṃyuge abhyavarṣac charaugheṇa meruṃ vṛṣṭyā yathāmbudaḥ
english: Seeing that hero slain, Aśvatthāman, the great car-warrior, rushed with speed against the grandson of Śini in the battle, and rained upon him a flood of arrows, as a cloud rains upon Meru.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃrabdhaṃ śaineyasya rathaṃ prati ghaṭotkaco 'bravīd rājan nādaṃ muktvā mahārathaḥ
english: As he furiously bore down upon the car of the grandson of Śini, Ghaṭotkaca, the great car-warrior, O king, loosing a roar, spoke.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha na me jīvan droṇaputra gamiṣyasi eṣa tvādya haniṣyāmi mahiṣaṃ skandarāḍ iva yuddhaśraddhām ahaṃ te 'dya vineṣyāmi raṇājire
english: 'Stand, stand! Thou shalt not escape me alive, O son of Droṇa. This day I shall slay thee as the lord Skanda slew the buffalo; this day, on the field of battle, I shall drive out thy appetite for war.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā roṣatāmrākṣo rākṣasaḥ paravīrahā drauṇim abhyadravat kruddho gajendram iva kesarī
english: Having spoken thus, the Rākṣasa, that slayer of hostile heroes, his eyes coppery with rage, rushed in wrath upon the son of Droṇa, as a lion upon a lordly elephant.

sanskrit: rathākṣamātrair iṣubhir abhyavarṣad ghaṭotkacaḥ rathinām ṛṣabhaṃ drauṇiṃ dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ
english: Ghaṭotkaca rained upon the son of Droṇa, that bull among car-warriors, arrows as large as chariot-axles, as a cloud rains down its torrents.

sanskrit: śaravṛṣṭiṃ tu tāṃ prāptāṃ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ śātayām āsa samare tarasā drauṇir utsmayan
english: But that downpour of arrows, as it came, the son of Droṇa, smiling, swiftly shattered in the battle with shafts like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatais tīkṣṇair marmabhedibhir āśugaiḥ samācinod rākṣasendraṃ ghaṭotkacam ariṃdama
english: Then with hundreds of sharp, swift arrows that pierce the vitals, O subduer of foes, he covered Ghaṭotkaca, the lord of the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa śarair ācitas tena rākṣaso raṇamūrdhani vyakāśata mahārāja śvāvic chalalito yathā
english: Studded all over with his arrows, that Rākṣasa, at the head of the battle, shone, O great king, like a porcupine bristling with its quills.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭo bhaimaseniḥ pratāpavān śarair avacakartograir drauṇiṃ vajrāśanisvanaiḥ
english: Then the valiant son of Bhīmasena, filled with rage, cut into the son of Droṇa with fierce arrows that sounded like the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: kṣuraprair ardhacandraiś ca nārācaiḥ saśilīmukhaiḥ varāhakarṇair nālīkais tīkṣṇaiś cāpi vikarṇibhiḥ
english: With razor-edged shafts and crescent-headed arrows, with iron shafts and bearded darts, with boar-eared and reed-like points, and with sharp barbed missiles.

sanskrit: tāṃ śastravṛṣṭim atulāṃ vajrāśanisamasvanām patantīm upari kruddho drauṇir avyathitendriyaḥ
english: That matchless rain of weapons, sounding like the thunderbolt, as it fell upon him, the son of Droṇa, undismayed of sense, in his wrath—

sanskrit: suduḥsahāṃ śarair ghorair divyāstrapratimantritaiḥ vyadhamat sa mahātejā mahābhrāṇīva mārutaḥ
english: —that hard-to-bear downpour he, of mighty energy, dispelled with dreadful arrows charged with celestial weapons, as the wind scatters great clouds.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe bāṇānāṃ saṃgrāmo 'nya ivābhavat ghorarūpo mahārāja yodhānāṃ harṣavardhanaḥ
english: Then in the sky there arose, as it were, another battle of arrows, dreadful of aspect, O great king, that heightened the joy of the warriors.

sanskrit: tato 'strasaṃgharṣakṛtair visphuliṅgaiḥ samantataḥ babhau niśāmukhe vyoma khadyotair iva saṃvṛtam
english: Then with the sparks struck up by the clash of weapons on every side, the sky at the onset of night shone as if covered with fireflies.

sanskrit: sa mārgaṇagaṇair drauṇir diśaḥ pracchādya sarvataḥ priyārthaṃ tava putrāṇāṃ rākṣasaṃ samavākirat
english: The son of Droṇa, veiling all the quarters round about with his hosts of arrows, to please your sons, overwhelmed the Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ drauṇirākṣasayor mṛdhe vigāḍhe rajanīmadhye śakraprahrādayor iva
english: Then in the dead of deep night there raged the combat between the son of Droṇa and the Rākṣasa, like that between Śakra and Prahrāda.

sanskrit: tato ghaṭotkaco bāṇair daśabhir drauṇim āhave jaghānorasi saṃkruddhaḥ kālajvalanasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, greatly enraged, struck the son of Droṇa on the breast in the fight with ten arrows resembling the fire of doom.

sanskrit: sa tair abhyāyatair viddho rākṣasena mahābalaḥ cacāla samare drauṇir vātanunna iva drumaḥ sa moham anusaṃprāpto dhvajayaṣṭiṃ samāśritaḥ
english: Pierced by those long shafts of the mighty Rākṣasa, the son of Droṇa reeled in the battle like a tree shaken by the wind, and, falling into a swoon, he clung to the staff of his banner.

sanskrit: tato hāhākṛtaṃ sainyaṃ tava sarvaṃ janādhipa hataṃ sma menire sarve tāvakās taṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Then all your army cried out in dismay, O ruler of men, and all your men deemed him slain, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathāvastham aśvatthāmānam āhave pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayāś caiva siṃhanādaṃ pracakrire
english: Seeing Aśvatthāman reduced to such a plight in the battle, the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas set up a leonine roar.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñām aśvatthāmā mahābalaḥ dhanuḥ prapīḍya vāmena kareṇāmitrakarśanaḥ
english: Then regaining his senses, Aśvatthāman of great strength, that grinder of foes, gripping his bow firmly with his left hand—

sanskrit: mumocākarṇapūrṇena dhanuṣā śaram uttamam yamadaṇḍopamaṃ ghoram uddiśyāśu ghaṭotkacam
english: —with the bow drawn full to the ear, loosed a surpassing arrow, dreadful as the rod of Yama, aimed swiftly at Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: sa bhittvā hṛdayaṃ tasya rākṣasasya śarottamaḥ viveśa vasudhām ugraḥ supuṅkhaḥ pṛthivīpate
english: That excellent shaft, cleaving the heart of that Rākṣasa, fierce and fair-feathered, entered the earth, O lord of the world.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja rathopastha upāviśat rākṣasendraḥ subalavān drauṇinā raṇamāninā
english: Deeply pierced, O great king, that lord of the Rākṣasas, mighty though he was, sank down upon the floor of his car, struck by the son of Droṇa, proud of his battle.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vimūḍhaṃ haiḍimbaṃ sārathis taṃ raṇājirāt drauṇeḥ sakāśāt saṃbhrāntas tv apaninye tvarānvitaḥ
english: Seeing the son of Hiḍimbā swooning, his charioteer, in alarm, swiftly bore him away from the field, out of the presence of the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tathā tu samare viddhvā rākṣasendraṃ ghaṭotkacam nanāda sumahānādaṃ droṇaputro mahābalaḥ
english: Having thus pierced Ghaṭotkaca, the lord of the Rākṣasas, in the battle, the son of Droṇa, of great might, sent forth a tremendous roar.

sanskrit: pūjitas tava putraiś ca sarvayodhaiś ca bhārata vapuṣā pratijajvāla madhyāhna iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Honoured by your sons and by all the warriors, O descendant of Bharata, he blazed forth in his body like the sun at noon.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tu yudhyantaṃ bhāradvājarathaṃ prati svayaṃ duryodhano rājā pratyavidhyac chitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And as Bhīmasena fought his way toward the car of the son of Bharadvāja, king Duryodhana himself pierced him in return with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaseno navabhiḥ śarair vivyādha māriṣa duryodhano 'pi viṃśatyā śarāṇāṃ pratyavidhyata
english: Bhīmasena pierced him with nine arrows, O sire, and Duryodhana too pierced him in return with twenty shafts.

sanskrit: tau sāyakair avacchannāv adṛśyetāṃ raṇājire meghajālasamācchannau nabhasīvendubhāskarau
english: The two of them, veiled with arrows, were seen on the field of battle like the moon and the sun in the sky shrouded by a mass of clouds.

sanskrit: atha duryodhano rājā bhīmaṃ vivyādha patribhiḥ pañcabhir bharataśreṣṭha tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Then king Duryodhana pierced Bhīma with five feathered shafts, O best of the Bhāratas, and cried, 'Stand! Stand!'

sanskrit: tasya bhīmo dhanuś chittvā dhvajaṃ ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha kauravaśreṣṭhaṃ navatyā nataparvaṇām
english: Bhīma, cutting off his bow and his banner with nine arrows, pierced that best of the Kauravas with ninety shafts of smooth joints.
